key_insight: Danus coordinates multiple mathematical-reasoning agents around a shared fact graph, letting verified claims accumulate into long, organized proofs.
engineering_relevance: The design offers a scalable memory-and-control pattern for long-horizon AI workflows where parallel search, verification, and provenance tracking must stay consistent.
method: Main agent plans, summarizes progress, and redirects search across workers.
Worker agents explore proof branches in parallel.
A stateless verifier admits only checked claims into a shared fact graph with proofs and dependencies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports six research-level case studies across algebraic geometry, singularity theory, and combinatorics, showing the system can build long, detailed proofs.
watch_item: Performance depends on reliable verification and clean dependency management; errors in admitted facts could propagate through the shared graph.
paper_title: Danus: Orchestrating Mathematical Reasoning Agents with Fact-Graph Memory
